title: The Noisy street outside
subtitle: 城市生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 城市生活（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）
meta: 主题语境：城市生活（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）　|　核心词汇：noisy　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 noisy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the coach wrote of ① a noisy street outside in the record, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② noisier than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the coach, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the noisy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the noisiest street outside anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the record for April 1964 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too noisy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the player who had come to help; the noisy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the whistle at the far stand, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a noisy crowd in the hall, and said that no player in his right mind would call it ⑥ as noisy as the crowd in the hall they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was noisy or not, and he said so.

By 1977 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something noisy, and nothing besides. The player from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite noisy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the noisy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1980, for the whole place, she wrote of another noisy street outside in the same record, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ noisier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The noisiest crowd in the hall in the whole field, she said in 1982, was the one she could never quite name; the noisy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 吵闹（前置定语 a noisy street outside：1970 年教练在赛事记录里记下的那件吵闹的街道）
B. adj. 吵闹／喧哗（比较级 noisier than：文中两处，一处比外面喧闹的街道，一处比预想）
C. adj. 吵闹／喧哗（最高级 the noisiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 吵闹（表语 too noisy to do：母亲觉得它太吵闹，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 喧哗（前置定语 a noisy crowd in the hall：叔叔把整件事称作一桩喧哗的人群）
F. adj. 喧哗（同级比较 as noisy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厅里喧哗的人群相比）
G. adj. 喧哗（后置定语 something noisy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 喧哗（受程度副词修饰 quite noisy：那位队员的评价）

items.q: a noisy crowd in the hall
The noisiest crowd in the hall in

answers.why: noisy 意为“吵闹”，1970 年教练在赛事记录里记下的是“一件吵闹的街道”，此处作前置定语 a noisy street outside。
noisy 意为“吵闹”，此处用比较级 noisier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
noisy 意为“吵闹”，赛事记录上 四月 那行字说它是球场里最吵闹的一件，故用最高级 the noisiest street outside。
noisy 意为“吵闹”，母亲认为这件东西“太吵闹了，谁也用不上”，too noisy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩喧哗的人群”，此处作前置定语 a noisy crowd in the hall。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厅里喧哗的人群一样喧哗”，同级比较用 as noisy as。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，赛事记录上那半行字要的是“喧哗的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something noisy。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，邻球场来的那位队员认为这套计划“相当喧哗”，quite 修饰原级 noisy。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，1980 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要喧哗”，故用比较级 noisier than。
noisy 意为“喧哗”，母亲 1982 年说的是“整个球场里最喧哗的那一桩”，故用最高级 the noisiest crowd in the hall。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1970 年，教练在赛事记录里记下了一件吵闹的街道。（a noisy street outside）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更吵闹。（noisier than …）
母亲觉得它太吵闹，谁也用不上。（too noisy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩喧哗的人群。（a noisy crowd in the hall）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厅里喧哗的人群一样喧哗。（as noisy as …）
到了 1977 年，赛事记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件喧哗的东西。（something noisy）
answers: In 1970 the coach wrote of a noisy street outside in the record.
Everybody said it was noisier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too noisy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a noisy crowd in the hall.
He said nobody would call it as noisy as the crowd in the hall they had once had.
By 1977 the record asked for nothing but something noisy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 noisy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1970 the coach wrote of a noisy street outside in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the noisiest street outside in the field, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too noisy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a noisy crowd in the hall, and nobody argued with him.
The player from the next field called the plan quite noisy, and everybody laughed.
The noisy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
